gaps.sentence: Studying abroad is a wonderful ___ to practise your Spanish.
gaps.hint: a situation that lets you do something; pattern: ___ to do
gaps.explanation: 'Opportunity to do something' means a chance a situation gives you; 'possibility' is not followed by 'to'.

gaps.sentence: The new law will ___ every driver in the country.
gaps.explanation: 'Affect' is the verb meaning to have an influence on; 'effect' is normally a noun meaning a result.

gaps.sentence: I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.
'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: This small car is very ___ to run.
gaps.explanation: 'Economical' means costing little or saving money; 'economic' relates to trade, industry or the economy.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: The government’s ___ policy has divided economists.
gaps.explanation: 'Economic' relates to the economy; 'economical' means saving money.

gaps.sentence: He gave a ___ summary of the 40-page report.
gaps.explanation: 'A brief summary' — adjective; 'briefly' is the adverb.
